title: Mirror-edge presence improved prediction of edge presence between two adult worm maps after count and cell controls
abstract: We tested whether a matching left-right connection adds prediction of chemical edge presence in a second adult C. elegans map. We used primary synapse records from Witvliet datasets 7 and 8. The sample had 170 bilateral neurons and 1706 or 1703 observed index edges. Logistic models used source-family holdout and controls for synapse count, source and target synapse totals, cell types and same-side wiring. Mirror-edge presence improved the held-out log score by 0.0413 and 0.0355 nats per edge in the two map directions. Nominal 95 percent source-family bootstrap intervals were 0.0243 to 0.0579 and 0.0205 to 0.0501. A reverse edge gave little benefit. The mirror gain remained with a two-synapse outcome or after removal of bilateral-partner edges. Both directions reuse the same two animals. Fixed-prediction intervals omit shared-target, refit and animal uncertainty. The result is a wiring marker in two maps, not proof of a mechanism or a relation to measured neural activity. Code, derived tables, exact source hashes and a retrieval recipe support reproduction.

display.caption: Mirror-edge presence improved prediction of an observed connection in the other adult. Error bars show nominal source-family bootstrap intervals with predictions fixed.
